item.title: Brahmin, wisdom is purified by virtue, virtue is purified by wisdom. Where there is virtue, there is wisdom; where there is wisdom, there is virtue.…
item.description:
Brahmin, wisdom is purified by virtue, virtue is purified by wisdom. Where there is virtue, there is wisdom; where there is wisdom, there is virtue. One with virtue certainly has wisdom; one with wisdom certainly has virtue. Virtue and wisdom are considered supreme in the world.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 5 – Kūṭadantasutta

item.title: Elder Nun Sañjā: Leaving home, going forth, I abandoned my children, Abandoned precious livestock, Abandoned greed and hatred, And regarding ignorance, I live in seclusion.…
item.description:
Elder Nun Sañjā:

Leaving home, going forth,
I abandoned my children,
Abandoned precious livestock,
Abandoned greed and hatred,
And regarding ignorance,
I live in seclusion.
Having conquered
The root of craving itself,
I live cooled,
Peaceful and calm.

From: Therīgāthā 1.18

item.title: ( Blessed One ) One who gives with faith, With a pure mind, Enjoys that food In this life and the next. Therefore, avoid stinginess,…
item.description:
( Blessed One )
One who gives with faith,
With a pure mind,
Enjoys that food
In this life and the next.
Therefore, avoid stinginess,
Give, remove the stain,
Beings still enjoy
Merit in the next life.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.23

item.title: Bhikkhus, as long as the bhikkhus do not delight in sleeping, then the bhikkhus will prosper and not decline.
item.description:
Bhikkhus, as long as the bhikkhus do not delight in sleeping, then the bhikkhus will prosper and not decline.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 16 – Mahāparinibbānasutta

item.title: Bhikkhus, there are five strands of sensual pleasure. What are the five? Forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, stimulating sensual…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, there are five strands of sensual pleasure. What are the five? Forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, stimulating sensual desire, enticing. Sounds cognizable by the ear ... (as above) ... odors cognizable by the nose ... flavors cognizable by the tongue ... tangibles cognizable by the body that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, stimulating sensual desire, enticing. Bhikkhus, these are the five strands of sensual pleasure.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 26 – Ariyapariyesanāsutta

item.title: And, bhikkhus, what is a person with a mind like a wound? Here, bhikkhus, a person is irritable and very resentful; even when spoken to…
item.description:
And, bhikkhus, what is a person with a mind like a wound? Here, bhikkhus, a person is irritable and very resentful; even when spoken to lightly, he becomes exasperated, angry, hostile, and displays irritation, hatred, and bitterness. Just as a festering wound, if struck by a stick or a shard, discharges even more pus, so too, bhikkhus, here a person is irritable and resentful. This, bhikkhus, is called a person who is like a festering wound.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.25

item.title: Bhikkhus, just as a skilled carpenter or his apprentice uses a small peg to knock out, drive out, and remove a larger peg; so too,…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, just as a skilled carpenter or his apprentice uses a small peg to knock out, drive out, and remove a larger peg; so too, bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu, by attending to a certain sign, gives rise to evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion, then that bhikkhu should attend to another sign connected with what is wholesome, different from that sign. By attending to another sign connected with what is wholesome, those evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion are abandoned and subside. Through their abandonment, his mind becomes inwardly steady, settled, unified, and concentrated.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 20 – Vitakkasaṇṭhānasutta

item.title: Bhikkhus, as long as a teacher lives over-attached to material things, being an heir to material things, and lives in connection with material things, this…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, as long as a teacher lives over-attached to material things, being an heir to material things, and lives in connection with material things, this bargain does not occur: 'We will do this thus, and thus we will not do that.' How much more so for the Tathāgata, bhikkhus, who lives completely unconnected with material things.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 70 – Kīṭāgirisutta

item.title: Bhikkhus, these four things are few, easily obtained, and blameless. What four? Among robes, the dust-heap rag is few, easily obtained, and blameless. Among foods,…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, these four things are few, easily obtained, and blameless. What four? Among robes, the dust-heap rag is few, easily obtained, and blameless. Among foods, the lump of almsfood is few, easily obtained, and blameless. Among lodgings, the foot of a tree is few, easily obtained, and blameless. Among medicines, fermented cow's urine is few, easily obtained, and blameless. These four things are few, easily obtained, and blameless. Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is content with these few, easily obtained things, I declare that this is a factor of asceticism for him.

Content with things that are few,
Easily obtained, and blameless,
Mind not disturbed
Regarding lodgings, robes, food and drink.
Not worried about the direction one should go,
The Dhamma proclaimed, conducive to asceticism,
He possesses them fully,
For a bhikkhu who knows contentment, who is not heedless.

From: Itivuttaka 101

item.title: There are these six things that are part of true knowledge. What six? The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception…
item.description:
There are these six things that are part of true knowledge. What six? The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of non-self in suffering, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation. These six things, bhikkhus, are part of true knowledge.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.35
